quizzes.title: Body Basics
quizzes.description: A friendly tour of the bones, organs and blood that keep us going.

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.note: The liver is the largest internal organ, but the skin is the largest overall.

questions.q: A typical adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
questions.note: Babies start with around 300 bones, many of which fuse together as they grow.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.note: An adult heart beats roughly 100,000 times a day.

questions.q: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.note: Accept "enamel"; it coats the crown of every tooth.

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.note: The femur, or thigh bone, is also the strongest bone in the body.

questions.q: Which blood cells contain haemoglobin and carry oxygen?
questions.note: Haemoglobin is rich in iron, which is what makes blood look red.

questions.q: The human heart has three chambers.
questions.note: It has four: two atria on top and two ventricles below.

questions.q: Tiny air sacs called alveoli are found in which organs?
questions.note: Alveoli are where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.

questions.q: What dome-shaped muscle below the lungs helps you breathe?
questions.note: Hiccups are caused by sudden involuntary spasms of the diaphragm.

questions.q: How many teeth does a typical adult have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.note: Children have 20 baby teeth before their adult teeth come through.

quizzes.title: Elementary, My Dear
quizzes.description: Symbols, gases, metals and the table that organises them all.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
questions.note: Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin word for iron.

questions.q: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.note: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.

questions.q: Diamond and graphite are both made of pure carbon.
questions.note: The difference is how the carbon atoms are arranged.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?
questions.note: Fe comes from the Latin word for iron, ferrum.

questions.q: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.note: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air; oxygen is about 21%.

questions.q: Which of these metals is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.note: Mercury's symbol, Hg, comes from its old name hydrargyrum, meaning liquid silver.

questions.q: The noble gases include neon, argon and chlorine.
questions.note: Chlorine is a halogen; helium, neon, argon, krypton and xenon are noble gases.

questions.q: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.note: A pH of 7 is neutral; lower is acidic and higher is alkaline.

questions.q: Sodium chloride is better known by what everyday name?
questions.note: Accept "table salt".

questions.q: Who published a famous early periodic table in 1869?
questions.note: Mendeleev left gaps for elements that hadn't been discovered yet, and predicted their properties.

quizzes.title: Eureka Moments
quizzes.description: The people behind the breakthroughs that changed everyday life.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.note: He proposed it in 1989 while working at CERN in Switzerland.

questions.q: Who built the first electric battery, the voltaic pile, in 1800?
questions.note: The unit of electrical potential, the volt, is named after him.

questions.q: The Wright brothers made their first powered flight in France.
questions.note: It was near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, USA, in December 1903.

questions.q: Which German introduced movable-type printing to Europe around 1440?
questions.note: Accept "Gutenberg"; his most famous work is the Gutenberg Bible.

questions.q: In which year did the Wright brothers make their first powered flight?
questions.note: The very first flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered about 37 metres.

questions.q: Who developed the first smallpox vaccine in 1796?
questions.note: The word vaccine comes from vacca, Latin for cow, after the cowpox Jenner used.

questions.q: Which inventor of dynamite left his fortune to fund famous annual prizes?
questions.note: Accept "Nobel"; the first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901.

questions.q: Which machine did James Watt famously improve in the 18th century?
questions.note: The unit of power, the watt, is named after him.

questions.q: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays.
questions.note: He discovered them in 1895 and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

questions.q: Which prolific inventor created the phonograph in 1877?
questions.note: Edison held more than 1,000 US patents.

quizzes.title: May the Force Be With You
quizzes.description: Units, particles, light and the laws that make the universe tick.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.note: One newton is roughly the weight of a small apple.

questions.q: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.note: The exact figure is 299,792,458 metres per second.

questions.q: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
questions.note: It is over four times faster in water than in air.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.note: Named after German physicist Georg Ohm; its symbol is the Greek letter omega.

questions.q: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.note: Violet has the shortest wavelength of the visible colours.

questions.q: What temperature is absolute zero in degrees Celsius?
questions.note: Absolute zero is 0 kelvin, or -459.67 °F.

questions.q: In a vacuum, a heavy object falls faster than a light one.
questions.note: Without air resistance, all objects fall with the same acceleration.

questions.q: Which scientist discovered the electron in 1897?
questions.note: James Chadwick discovered the neutron later, in 1932.

questions.q: The unit of frequency, one cycle per second, is named after which physicist?
questions.note: Heinrich Hertz was the first to prove radio waves exist.

questions.q: What is the bending of light as it passes from one material to another called?
questions.note: Refraction is why a straw looks bent in a glass of water.
